key_insight: Differentiating through a simulated cylinder wake enables closed-loop policy optimisation that strongly suppresses vortex shedding with only eight policy updates.
engineering_relevance: Simulation gradients offer a potentially interaction-efficient route to feedback flow control with synthetic jets and sparse local velocity sensing.
method: Map local velocity measurements to synthetic-jet amplitude with a feedback policy.
Backpropagate control-loss gradients through differentiable flow simulation to update policy parameters.
Test feedback dependence, activation phases, disturbance recovery, rewards and sensor choices.
evidence_signal: In a two-dimensional confined wake at Reynolds number 100, eight updates using about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation achieved approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations.
watch_item: Results are limited to a two-dimensional simulated wake at Reynolds number 100; robustness in three-dimensional, higher-Reynolds-number or physical flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
